source_document: KMIPKIT-SRC-spec: Key Management Interoperability Protocol Specification Version 2.1
statement: Derived test (not an official OASIS test case). Use Undo, Stop, or Continue as the option value. KMIPKIT-DEC-002 accepts assigned outbound values and preserves raw decoded values without claiming the Table 435 extension allocation invalid.

The high-level `kmipkit-client::Client::execute` API MUST be synchronous and accept only a closed set of concrete typed KMIP request values. This initial feature includes only typed Discover Versions request items and MUST NOT accept a generic TTLV `Item`/`Structure`, raw message bytes, or caller-implemented serialization/conversion hooks. The separately documented low-level `kmipkit-transport::Transport::exchange` API may exchange caller-supplied bytes and return a zeroizing raw-response wrapper under ADR-0014; it is not re-exported by the top-level facade, performs no KMIP validation or encoding/decoding, and carries no typed-client guarantee.

The initial typed operation MUST implement Discover Versions request and response fields in OASIS §6.1.16, Tables 211–213. A request MUST advertise the KMIPKit-supported version `(2,1)` in decreasing preference order. Since the caller's offered list contains only `(2,1)`, a successful response payload MUST be empty or contain only `(2,1)`; any other returned version is a server conformance violation and MUST be rejected. The operation MUST be explicit and MUST NOT be called as an implicit preflight.

The execution layer MUST use KMIPKIT-0005's bounded decoder/private writer and KMIPKIT-0006's message/batch model without creating an alternate codec or message representation. All per-call codec limits MUST flow through unchanged by borrowed reference.

Every outgoing request and accepted response MUST use Protocol Version 2.1 under ADR-0002. Other major/minor pairs MUST be rejected. The implementation and documentation MUST identify this as the product-scope exception `KMIPKIT-DISC-022`, not as same-major backward compatibility.

The low-level transport boundary MUST synchronously exchange caller-supplied request bytes and a bounded response without logging or formatting request/response contents. On success it MUST return a `TransportResponse` whose drop zeroizes the initialized byte range in its current owned allocation before release and whose `Debug` output is redacted. On error it MUST zeroize the initialized byte range of each KMIPKit-owned partial or temporary response allocation before release and before returning a payload-free, redacted `TransportError` with delivery state. Spare or uninitialized capacity is outside these guarantees. An earlier allocation released by response-buffer growth, and every prior allocation used for a growing KMIPKit-owned request copy, MUST be zeroized before that allocation is released. Caller-created copies and copies owned by TLS, the operating system, or third-party transport libraries are outside KMIPKit's zeroization guarantee. Each concrete adapter MUST prevent response-buffer reallocation after response bytes have been stored or zeroize each prior/temporary allocation before release; its specification MUST require tests proving the selected allocation-cleanup strategy on success and error paths and document external-library copy limitations. The transport MUST NOT retain request bytes beyond the synchronous exchange and MUST zeroize KMIPKit-owned temporary request copies before release. The deterministic test transport MUST redact its script and transport `Debug` output and MUST zeroize KMIP-owned response fixture bytes after success, partial-read failure, or drop before exchange. Each concrete adapter specification MUST require applicable request nonlogging, nonretention, and temporary-copy cleanup tests. The caller owns the input buffer; direct callers also own the returned response wrapper and any copies they explicitly make. This low-level API provides no KMIP validation or typed-client guarantee. The deterministic fake MUST support partial-write behavior and report monotonic `RequestDeliveryState` transitions. No live network backend is in scope.

The response MUST be validated against the request before being returned: operation matches, item cardinality and identities match, required IDs are echoed, and reordered items are associated by their IDs. Duplicate, missing, or unexpected response items MUST fail closed. Any stricter project validation MUST be identified separately from the exact OASIS SHALLs.

The client MUST validate outbound Asynchronous Indicator values against Table 432 and §11.3, preserving assigned and extension-range values while rejecting unassigned values outside those ranges. For Batch Error Continuation, the client MUST enforce option presence/cardinality and MUST reject it on a single-item batch. Under project policy `KMIPKIT-DEC-002`, outbound requests in this slice accept only the three assigned values; the generic model continues to preserve all raw Enumeration values. This decision does not claim that Table 435's extension allocation is invalid under OASIS. The client MUST NOT infer Continue/Undo execution or rollback effects while `KMIPKIT-DISC-001` is unresolved.

The client MUST represent completed and Pending item results. It MUST accept Pending only when the request's effective Asynchronous Indicator permits it. A Pending result missing the required Asynchronous Correlation Value defined by the accepted KMIPKIT-0006 model MUST be rejected; when present, its opaque bytes MUST be preserved exactly through the `Client::execute` result for later explicit operations. An extension-range indicator MUST NOT be assumed to permit Pending without registered semantics. Poll, Cancel, Process, and automatic waiting remain out of scope.

The client MUST enforce the configured response-byte ceiling before decoding, and MUST pass the same configured `CodecLimits` reference to encoding and decoding without cloning or reconstructing it. It MUST preserve the difference between the peer-visible Maximum Response Size field and the local decoder/transport limits. Under KMIPKit policy, Discover Versions MUST omit the peer-visible field because this operation is not classified as likely-large. Every later operation spec MUST assess OASIS §9.12's large-response recommendation and define/test peer-size behavior where appropriate.

An unrecognized critical Message Extension MUST reject the whole message as required by OASIS §9.13. Unknown non-critical extension data MUST be preserved under KMIPKit project policy (`AGENTS.md` §9; OASIS permits processing it as absent). This initial feature registers no recognized critical extensions and MUST NOT claim vendor critical-extension support.

The request's private encoded owner MUST remain alive for the full synchronous transport exchange and be zeroized after drop. The production writer MUST be private to the client execution module, callable only by `Client::execute`, and require a private `OperationEncodingPermit` whose constructor and only mint site are in the same execute-owning module. There MUST be exactly one production permit mint site and writer callsite.

`Client::execute` MUST use a closed typed request surface and MUST expose no public generic encoder or caller-selected raw TTLV body. This does not prohibit the separately documented low-level transport byte-exchange API under ADR-0014. The candidate production callsite and its owner-through-transport integration test MUST be in the same change. CI MUST pass the test before merge, enablement, or release, as required by ADR-0012 and KMIPKIT-0005 FR-013.

Failures MUST preserve accurate delivery state and safe, sanitized cause categories. They MUST NOT retain or display arbitrary original source text, which may contain untrusted or sensitive data. Before an error is returned, each KMIPKit-owned partial response allocation MUST have its initialized byte range zeroized; FR-005 defines the limits for spare capacity, prior allocations, and external copies. Neither error storage nor formatting may expose response contents. Execution MUST NOT automatically retry, fail over, poll, or resubmit. Formatting, logging, and errors MUST redact request/response bytes and all secret material.

Each normative requirement and project invariant MUST have a stable identifier linked to its exact OASIS/catalog source or policy, implementation location, and executable test before implementation completion. Derived tests MUST NOT be labeled official OASIS test vectors.

The client MUST preserve an optional caller-supplied request Time Stamp as Date-Time exactly and MUST omit it when absent. This feature MUST NOT synthesize a request Time Stamp from a countdown timer. Countdown-derived outgoing Time Stamp generation is outside this feature's scope under OD-004; a future feature that proposes it must define its time-source policy and normative basis. This feature does not claim that OASIS §9.20 authorizes converting a countdown timer into the outgoing field. Deterministic tests MUST cover exact preservation and omission. The supplied value MUST NOT appear in supported diagnostics, error formatting or exposed error-source chains, and MUST NOT be logged.

A client-initiated request MUST NOT expose a setter for or emit Server Correlation Value. An optional Client Correlation Value MUST remain distinct from Unique Batch Item ID and MUST NOT be used as the response batch-item match key.

The Asynchronous Correlation Value MUST be treated as capability-like sensitive metadata: preserve its exact bytes for explicit later operations, expose them only through an explicit borrowed accessor, redact them from `Debug`, `Display`, errors, and logs, and retain KMIPKit-owned copies in zeroizing storage until drop. The implementation MUST NOT create an ordinary unzeroized duplicate.
Every outgoing request and accepted response header is KMIP 2.1; acceptance passes an iff-property over signed 32-bit major/minor values.

The deterministic fake demonstrates valid explicit Discover Versions success, empty version list, KMIP error result, reordered correlated batch, mixed Pending/completed results, exact Asynchronous Correlation Value byte preservation, and rejection of malformed batch identity or Pending results missing that value.

The compliant fake stops retaining response bytes at the configured cap; the client rejects an oversized `TransportResponse` returned by a deliberately non-compliant fake before decoder invocation; successful wrapper drop and partial-read error cleanup zeroize every initialized byte in the current KMIPKit-owned response allocation; the peer Maximum Response Size field is absent for Discover Versions; and the exact same borrowed `CodecLimits` reference reaches encoder and decoder. These fake tests do not claim that spare/uninitialized capacity, previous allocations, or external-library copies are cleared and are not evidence about production adapter allocation behavior. Each adapter specification must define and test its response-buffer growth strategy and cleanup on success and errors.

Production source audit finds exactly one permit mint and one private writer callsite, both in the `Client::execute` path; no other `kmipkit-client` path can submit generic TTLV. The separate public transport byte-exchange exception is documented under ADR-0014.

Fake transport tests prove delivery state for pre-send, partial-write, and response-started failures, no retry, request-owner lifetime through exchange return, zeroization after drop, and redaction in `Debug`, `Display`, and any exposed typed error-source chain.

Changed client/protocol/transport lines meet at least 95% line coverage and every in-scope normative or policy requirement has an implementation and executable-test link before implementation PR review.

A caller-supplied request Time Stamp is preserved exactly, an absent value remains absent, and no Time Stamp is synthesized; the supplied value is absent from supported diagnostics, error formatting and exposed error-source chains, and any logging on the execution path; no Server Correlation Value is emitted.

A Pending Asynchronous Correlation Value survives unchanged while its result is live and is available only through its explicit borrowed accessor; a sentinel is absent from `Debug`, `Display`, errors, and captured logs, and KMIPKit-owned storage is zeroized when dropped without an ordinary unzeroized duplicate.

Direct low-level fake exchanges carrying a unique request sentinel prove that it is absent from captured logs and from fake-retained state after both success and error. Observers confirm that KMIPKit-owned temporary request copies and scripted response fixtures have every initialized byte zeroed before deallocation, including an unconsumed fixture dropped before exchange. This verifies the fake contract only; each concrete adapter specification must assign applicable request nonlogging, nonretention, response-allocation cleanup, and temporary-copy tests and document external-library copies.
